title: Extract Block Maxima from Time Series — block_maxima
text: ## Overview block maxima method one two classical approaches extreme value theory (EVT), along peaks--threshold (POT). transforms time series length n approximately n/block_size maxima, appropriate conditions converge Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) distribution. ## Use Block Maxima Block maxima appropriate : - want analyze extremes fixed time periods (e.g., annual maxima) - data naturally divides meaningful blocks (seasons, years, cycles) - prefer working fewer, independent observations - Theoretical conditions GEV approximation met ## Comparison Peaks--Threshold **Advantages**: - Simpler conceptually - Automatically provides approximately independent observations - Well-established theory inference procedures **Disadvantages**: - Less efficient: discards non-maximal values block - Requires choosing block size (bias-variance tradeoff) - May suitable short time series Generally, POT preferred long time series want extract information data. ## Choosing Block Size Block size selection involves tradeoff: - **small**: Maxima may independent, GEV approximation poor - **large**: blocks, high variance estimates Rules thumb: - least 20-50 blocks reliable estimation - Blocks span "natural" time scale system - chaotic systems: consider correlation time Lyapunov timescale

title: Extract Block Maxima from Time Series — block_maxima

title: Decluster threshold exceedances — decluster
text: Two consecutive exceedances belong cluster time-index gap `run_length`. cluster reduced single number via `stat`: - `"max"` (default): block-maximum-style representative, standard   choice GPD declustering. - `"first"` / `"last"`: preserve timing cluster onset / decay. - `"sum"`: cluster intensity (sum exceedances zero). - `"mean"`: average exceedance within cluster. chaotic dynamical systems extremes typically cluster (extremal index \(\theta < 1\)), applying `fit_gpd` directly raw exceedances underestimates scale biases shape parameter. Declustering first restores IID assumption GPD asymptotics rest .

title: Estimate Extremal Index Using Runs Method — extremal_index_runs
text: ## Overview extremal index θ ∈ (0, 1] fundamental parameter extreme value theory dependent sequences. measures tendency extreme values appear clusters rather individually. ## Interpretation θ - **θ = 1**: Extreme values occur independently (like IID data) - **θ < 1**: Extreme values cluster together - **θ = 0.5**: average, extremes appear pairs - **θ = 0.33**: average, extremes appear triplets chaotic dynamical systems, θ typically less 1 system's deterministic nature causes extreme events cluster. value θ depends system's mixing properties choice threshold. ## Runs Method runs estimator defines clusters based gaps exceedances. Two exceedances belong cluster separated `run_length` time steps. estimator : $$\hat{\theta} = \frac{N_c}{N}$$ \(N_c\) number clusters N total number exceedances. ## Choosing run_length choice `run_length` affects estimate: - **small**: May split natural clusters, overestimating θ - **large**: May merge distinct clusters, underestimating θ Common choices: - run_length = 1 2 applications - run_length based ACF structure (first zero crossing) - run_length based extremal index diagnostics ## Relationship Return Times extremal index affects return times extreme events. threshold u exceedance probability p, mean cluster size 1/θ mean inter-cluster time 1/(θp).

title: Estimate Extremal Index Using Runs Method — extremal_index_runs

title: Fit Generalized Extreme Value Distribution to Block Maxima — fit_gev
text: ## Overview GEV distribution combines three classical extreme value distributions (Gumbel, Fréchet, Weibull) single family. parameterized location (μ), scale (σ > 0), shape (ξ) parameters. function provides convenient wrapper uses `evd::fgev()` evd package available, otherwise falls back `ismev::gev.fit()`. implementations use maximum likelihood estimation. ## GEV Distribution cumulative distribution function : $$G(z) = \exp\{-(1 + \xi z)^{-1/\xi}\}$$ z = (x - μ)/σ support depends ξ. ## Shape Parameter Interpretation shape parameter ξ controls tail behavior: - **ξ > 0**: Fréchet type (heavy tail, power-law decay) - **ξ = 0**: Gumbel type (light tail, exponential decay) - **ξ < 0**: Weibull type (bounded tail, finite upper endpoint) chaotic systems, ξ often close zero slightly negative, depending system's dynamics observable studied. ## Model Diagnostics fitting, always check: - Probability plots (Q-Q, P-P) - Return level plots - Confidence intervals parameters - Likelihood-based diagnostics

text: Estimates full Lyapunov spectrum \(\lambda_1 \ge \ldots \ge \lambda_d\) discrete map \(x \mapsto f(x)\) via Benettin's QR algorithm: step linearised tangent map \(J(x_k)\) acts orthonormal basis \(V_k\), running average log diagonal QR factor gives Lyapunov exponents.

title: Lyapunov spectrum of a discrete map — lyapunov_spectrum
text: map_fn Function. Takes numeric vector `x` length `d` returns next state, also length `d`. jacobian_fn Function. Takes `x` returns \(d \times d\) Jacobian matrix \(J(x) = \partial f / \partial x\). x0 Numeric vector length `d`. Initial condition. n_iter Integer (\(\ge 1\)). Number iterations average spectrum . Defaults 5000. transient Integer (\(\ge 0\)). Iterations orbit-evolution starting QR sweep. Defaults 1000.

title: Lyapunov spectrum of a discrete map — lyapunov_spectrum
text: Numeric vector length `d` holding Lyapunov exponents   decreasing order.

title: Lyapunov spectrum of a discrete map — lyapunov_spectrum
text: chaotic system, \(\lambda_1 > 0\). sum spectrum equals time-averaged log determinant Jacobian, area-contracting maps (\(|\det J| < 1\)) sum negative. Implementation notes: - QR factorisation sign-corrected diagonal `R`   positive. keeps basis update deterministic avoids   sign ambiguity otherwise show every step. - short transient orbit-iteration discards initial   alignment basis unstable manifold; defaults   1000 iterations, plenty canonical maps.

title: Lyapunov spectrum of a continuous-time flow — lyapunov_spectrum_continuous
text: Standard Benettin/Wolf approach flows. orbit \(d \times d\) tangent matrix \(V\) advanced RK4 step, sharing intermediate evaluations Jacobian half- full-step states. QR re-orthogonalisation prevents \(V\) collapsing onto leading expanding direction; time-averaged diagonal logs \(R\) give spectrum. Sum check: Lorenz canonical parameters spectrum approximately \((0.906, 0, -14.572)\) sum \(-\sigma - 1 - \beta = -13.667\); Rossler \((0.2, 0.2, 5.7)\) approximately \((0.0714, 0, -5.392)\). middle exponent identically zero direction flow.
